source_snapshot.test_name: CPU over temperature via peltier device / remove heatsink
source_snapshot.items: CPU over temperature via peltier device / remove heatsink
source_snapshot.procedure: Boot the supported OS, remove the heatsink or use a Peltier device to slowly heat the configured CPU through TWarning and TCritical, then continue heating until the system resets while monitoring the BMC Web UI.
source_snapshot.criteria: Shutdown once TCritical is reached; CPU-specific BMC over-temperature log; applicable temperature LED, LCD, CPU lightpath and front fault light; after reboot, corresponding UEFI SEL CPU over-temperature and system-reset evidence.
source_snapshot.deepseek_finding: DeepSeek correctly identifies the physical thermal injection as unavailable to an agent but treats the whole case as non-automatable and does not separate manual stimulus from automatable telemetry and log correlation.

original_test_intent.purpose: Validate the selected CPU's platform over-temperature warning/critical detection, protective power transition, BMC/UEFI event correlation and applicable physical fault indications under a deliberately controlled loss or reversal of normal cooling.
original_test_intent.target: One platform-authorized CPU/socket, its BMC thermal sensor/event path, system power protection, available diagnostic LEDs/LCD/lightpath and BMC/UEFI SEL evidence.
original_test_intent.scope: A qualified operator applies one approved Peltier or heatsink-removal fault-injection method while automation collects read-only telemetry and logs. The test is not a software CPU stress test and cannot be generalized across Intel/AMD or server designs without the target recipe.
original_test_intent.operation: After resolving the expected power transition and hard stop, preserve baseline logs, identify CPU/sensor/thresholds, start synchronized BMC/OS/independent-probe collection, have the operator slowly apply the approved stimulus, record warning/critical crossings and protection response, stop heat at the approved limit, inspect physical indicators, restore cooling, recover only after safety approval and correlate BMC/UEFI/OS evidence.
original_test_intent.duration_and_iterations: The workbook estimates 30 attended and 10 machine minutes and describes one controlled thermal event; it gives no repeat count.
original_test_intent.expected_result: The selected CPU reaches documented platform warning and critical conditions in the required order, produces the specified CPU-specific events/indicators, and enters the exact owner-defined protective power state without crossing the independent damage limit; recovery restores normal cooling and health. The current source conflicts on shutdown versus reset timing.
original_test_intent.required_evidence: Platform/CPU/socket and firmware identity; authoritative threshold/event/power-policy mapping; selected fault method/SOP/approval; fixture and independent probe calibration; synchronized BMC/OS temperature timeline; warning/critical events; exact power transition; BMC and UEFI SEL; available physical indicators; cooling restoration, inspection and post-recovery health.
ambiguities: Procedure says to continue heating after TCritical until system reset, while Criteria says the system shuts down once TCritical is reached.
The source does not define whether reset means a warm reset, cold restart, power-off caused by thermal protection, or an observed loss of service.
TWarning and TCritical values, sensor semantics and CPU/socket mapping are absent.
The source offers heatsink removal or Peltier stimulus without choosing a platform-qualified method or defining condensation, contact, ramp-rate and hard damage limits.
LED/LCD/lightpath requirements are conditional on platform hardware but the exact applicability map is absent.
source_conflicts: The required protective state and trigger point conflict between Procedure and Criteria: continue-to-reset versus shutdown-at-TCritical.

v2_review_conclusion.finding: V2 correctly reclassifies the case as a hybrid manual-stimulus/automated-evidence workflow and adds strong fixture, independent measurement, approval, stop and recovery controls. It does not formally surface the source's shutdown-versus-reset conflict and says to stop at the protective response even though the source requires continued heating until reset, leaving completion and acceptance ambiguous.

applicable_history.decision: The historical NO decision reflects inability of the agent to perform physical injection, not inability to automate monitoring and evidence; V3 retains the user-confirmed hybrid boundary and does not return the case to blanket MANUAL ONLY.

v3_review_conclusion.summary: Retain V2's hybrid classification and safety controls, but block physical injection until the platform owner defines the exact warning/critical semantics, protective power state and hard stop. Read-only inventory and baseline collection can proceed now.

available_now: The intended CPU thermal-protection and evidence domains are identifiable.
BMC sensor/threshold inventory, current health, logs and indicator availability can be collected read-only.
Automation can later timestamp and correlate telemetry, power state and logs while a human controls the fixture.
missing_inputs: Authoritative CPU/socket, BMC sensor mapping, TWarning/TCritical definitions, expected protective state and accepted event/indicator map.

A platform-qualified choice between Peltier and heatsink-removal procedures, including fixture, ramp rate, independent limit, ESD/condensation controls, emergency stop, cooling restoration and inspection.
Explicit high-risk approval, staffed operator, recovery console and maintenance window.
execution_readiness_detail.input_owner: The platform thermal/BMC owner resolves thresholds, power-policy and indicator expectations; the qualified lab owner supplies/approves the physical SOP and calibrated package; the system owner authorizes outage and recovery.
safe_read_only_work_before_closure: Capture platform/CPU/socket/firmware inventory, BMC sensor names/thresholds, current temperatures, power policy, existing BMC/OS/UEFI logs and physical-indicator applicability without clearing anything.
prohibited_until_closed: Do not remove a heatsink, energize a Peltier fixture, heat the CPU, impose load, clear logs, guess thresholds, equate BMC thresholds with CPU TCC/THERMTRIP, continue after an undefined protection response, reboot or repeat the event.
execution_readiness_detail.closure_verification: Approve a revision that names one CPU/socket and physical method, reconciles shutdown/reset semantics, defines independent ramp/temperature/time hard stops and event/indicator acceptance, demonstrates emergency stop/recovery readiness, and records explicit owner approval.

revision_candidate.test_name: Controlled CPU Over-Temperature Protection and Evidence Correlation
revision_candidate.purpose: Validate one specified CPU/socket's platform warning, critical protection, power-state response and BMC/UEFI/physical indication chain under an owner-approved controlled thermal fault.
revision_candidate.applicable_platform_environment: Only the exact server, CPU family, socket, BMC/BIOS firmware and thermal design covered by the approved platform recipe; do not transfer thresholds or signal behavior across Intel, AMD or different server designs.
revision_candidate.target_scope: One authorized CPU/socket and one controlled thermal event using one approved physical method, plus its BMC/OS/UEFI and applicable panel indication paths.
revision_candidate.required_inputs: Resolved shutdown/reset expectation; CPU/socket and sensor map; TWarning/TCritical and protection policy; applicable event/LED/LCD/lightpath criteria; qualified physical SOP/fixture; calibrated independent probe; ramp and hard-stop limits; operator, ESD/condensation controls, approval, maintenance, emergency stop and recovery plan.
revision_candidate.test_command_procedure_intent: Before any injection, collect preserved baseline inventory, thresholds, sensors, power state and logs. Under the separately approved physical SOP, a qualified operator applies the selected stimulus slowly while the agent records synchronized BMC/OS and independent-probe data. Record TWarning and TCritical events and the owner-defined protective transition; immediately remove stimulus at the specified response or hard stop. After safe cooling and operator approval, restore the heatsink/thermal path, inspect, recover, collect BMC/UEFI/OS and physical-indicator evidence and verify normal health. Do not execute until shutdown-versus-reset is resolved.
revision_candidate.preconditions: Exact platform/CPU and supported OS verified; normal baseline health; logs preserved; no conflicting workload; threshold/policy and indicator map approved; fixture/probe calibrated; physical operator and emergency stop present; remote/local recovery available; explicit outage/fault approval recorded.
revision_candidate.expected_evidence: Identity and approved recipe; selected method and calibration; synchronized independent/BMC temperature trajectory; warning/critical timestamps; exact power-state transition; CPU-specific BMC and UEFI SEL; OS loss/recovery context; applicable LED/LCD/lightpath/fault-light photos; hard-stop compliance; restored cooling and post-event health/inspection.
revision_candidate.acceptance_reference: The exact platform thermal/BMC/BIOS specification and approved lab SOP. Processor-vendor thermal documentation may explain TCC/THERMTRIP behavior but cannot substitute for the server's TWarning/TCritical, power-policy or indication requirements.
revision_candidate.safety_restrictions: No remote agent may manipulate the fixture or heatsink. Never run with unresolved power semantics, absent independent sensing, no emergency stop, guessed thresholds, excessive ramp, condensation/ESD risk, missing recovery, or continued heating after the approved response/hard stop. Preserve logs and do not repeat automatically.
revision_candidate.human_approval_requirements: A qualified thermal operator and platform/system owners must approve the exact CPU, method, limits, expected power transition, outage, indicators and recovery immediately before injection.
revision_candidate.manual_boundaries: The operator owns all physical setup, stimulus, emergency stop, indicator observation, cooling restoration and inspection. The agent only collects authorized read-only telemetry/logs and correlates evidence; it cannot declare hardware safe.
revision_candidate.recovery_requirements: Remove stimulus, restore the qualified heatsink/thermal interface, allow controlled cooling, inspect socket/board/fixture, recover power only after approval, collect persistent evidence and verify temperatures/fans/sensors/CPU inventory and system health. Escalate and quarantine on failed protection or abnormal health.
revision_candidate.stop_conditions: Unresolved shutdown/reset expectation; wrong CPU/sensor; abnormal baseline; calibration/fixture/operator/approval/recovery gap; independent probe divergence; excessive ramp; condensation/ESD concern; unexpected event order; missed documented protection point; approach to hard limit; wrong power transition; smoke/odor/visual anomaly; lost monitoring; or any post-event abnormality.

identified_defects: Source Procedure and Criteria conflict on reset versus shutdown and on when heat must stop.
Threshold values and BMC-sensor-to-CPU mapping are absent.
Two materially different physical fault methods are offered without a qualified selection/SOP.
V2 improves safety but leaves the completion transition ambiguous.
The source clears logs even though event correlation depends on preserved pre/post evidence.
reason_for_change: Preserve V2's valid hybrid automation model while preventing a qualified operator from following mutually incompatible continue-heating and shutdown-at-critical instructions during a potentially destructive CPU thermal event.

new_technical_evidence.title: Intel Xeon Processor Scalable Family Thermal Mechanical Specifications and Design Guide
new_technical_evidence.applicability: Illustrative only when the selected target is the covered Intel Xeon Scalable family; not applicable to unknown or AMD CPUs
new_technical_evidence.supports: TCC first attempts to control temperature/power during excursions, while a more severe uncontrolled excursion can reach THERMTRIP_N and shutdown where data integrity is no longer assured. Therefore warning/critical BMC thresholds and catastrophic processor trip cannot be treated as interchangeable without the platform map.
new_technical_evidence.remaining_uncertainty: The selected CPU vendor/model, server power policy, BMC thresholds and exact shutdown/reset behavior are not supplied.

removed_ambiguities: Separates BMC warning/critical thresholds from processor TCC/THERMTRIP semantics.
Requires one selected physical method and one CPU/socket.
Makes reconciliation of shutdown versus reset a precondition rather than guessing completion.
resolved_blockers: V2 already established that automated evidence collection can coexist with a manual physical stimulus, so the case is not blanket MANUAL ONLY.
remaining_blockers: Protective power transition and stopping point conflict in the source.
Platform thresholds/sensor/indicator mapping and qualified physical SOP are missing.
High-risk approval, operator, calibrated fixture and recovery readiness are not established.
objective_improvement_over_v2: V3 keeps V2's strong hybrid safety model but exposes the shutdown/reset contradiction, prevents conflation of platform and processor thermal thresholds, and turns the exact stop/recovery behavior into an auditable release condition.

agent_understanding_result.notes: The contract-only validator recovered the exact one-CPU/one-event purpose, platform boundary, unresolved shutdown/reset input, safe baseline reads, operator-only physical actions, approval, evidence, hard stops and recovery. It explicitly refused execution before inputs/approval, prohibited agent fixture manipulation and automatic repeats, and did not treat recovery as protection PASS. No document, platform-handoff or model-planning failure was found.

per_case_integrity_check.source_specific_purpose_fact: Functionality row 1422 requires staged CPU heating through TWarning/TCritical and multi-layer physical/BMC/UEFI evidence, but conflicts on shutdown versus reset.
per_case_integrity_check.source_specific_v2_comparison: V2 correctly enables hybrid monitoring but does not formally block on the source's incompatible transition/stopping instructions.
per_case_integrity_check.source_specific_safety_evidence_decision: Permit read-only baselining; prohibit all thermal injection until the exact target, method, thresholds, power response, hard stop, approval and recovery are resolved.
